cards.subject: Ameth'Aran and Bashal'Aran
lines: Azshara founded twin cities here, and they were the pinnacle of night elf civilisation. They stood on the shore of the Well of Eternity.
The Sundering put the sea where the Well was. Every ruin in this zone is that one night.

cards.subject: The cat statues
lines: The stone cats in the northern ruins can be looted. Usually it is junk.
Sometimes a Ghost Saber spawns on top of you — a spectral frostsaber that looks permanently stealthed, and one of vanilla's famous hunter tames.
A freshly tamed one keeps its spawn timer and drops dead a few minutes later. Once. Then it is fine.

cards.subject: Blackfathom Deeps
lines: In early development the dungeon sat in the Ruins of Mathystra, here in northern Darkshore. It was moved to Ashenvale before release.
Darkshore has no dungeon and no battleground — one of very few zones with neither.
It was supposed to have one, and you are standing in where it was.

cards.subject: Athrikus Narassin
lines: Azshara posted him here to govern the twin cities. He was loyal at first, and then he grew bored of his post.
Ten thousand years later he is still in that tower, running the Cult of the Dark Strand.
He is also why the ruins are haunted: he trapped his own people's souls in gems, and burns them to power himself.

cards.subject: Asterion
lines: Athrikus's own second, the resident mage of Bashal'Aran, sealed inside an Ancient Moonstone Seal. Nothing ever says why.
Dying did not help. He found, to his horror, that even as a specter he was still imprisoned.
Ten thousand years, and it ends when a level twenty breaks the stone.

cards.subject: Auberdine's signposts
lines: A night elf town that reads as a port first: unusually well lit for a kaldorei settlement, with signs in two languages.
Dwarves, gnomes, humans and high elves all trade here.
There is a dwarven smithy in it.

cards.subject: Two boats, not three
lines: The Moonspray to Rut'theran Village, the Bravery to Menethil Harbor. That is the whole timetable.
Elune's Blessing to Azuremyst is a Burning Crusade addition and that pier does not run yet.
Auberdine is the only settlement in the zone and the Alliance's main port in northern Kalimdor. Everything crossing the sea comes through this one dock.

cards.subject: The air, not the mobs
lines: Darkshore was infamous for how many of its quests are underwater.
It only became survivable when the breath timer went to three minutes.
Most of what kills you here is the surface being further away than you thought.

cards.subject: The Blackwood
lines: The furbolgs here were uncultured but friendly to the night elves. Their time in the ruins turned many of them feral.
The taint bleeding down out of Felwood poisoned the zone's wildlife along with them.
You are not clearing a camp of monsters. You are clearing a camp of neighbours.

cards.subject: Onu
lines: He is not scenery. He is an Ancient of Lore, written slow and patient on purpose as the counterweight to Fandral Staghelm's hurry.
He talks to you at the Master's Glaive from where he is rooted, at the other end of the zone.
"Hum, hrm. A powerful reagent for one so young...birth is as powerful as death."

cards.subject: The Twilight's Hammer, in 1.12
lines: Everybody assumes the cult at the Glaive is Cataclysm. It is not. A level twenty quest, deleted from the game in 4.0.3a, says so.
A parchment taken from the Glaive comes back tainted by the corruption of the Twilight's Hammer.
"The cult is using ancient elven magic to bring their old masters back." Ten years before Deathwing.

cards.subject: The Master's Glaive
lines: The huge shell at the bottom of the zone is not architecture. It is the skull of Soggoth the Slitherer, a herald of the Old Gods.
The glaive is the sword still in its crown. About twenty titan-sent stone giants died here; only Kronn survived.
Nobody knows why the blade was left in. Likeliest answer: pulling it out lets the thing grow back.
